output_json.diff_review: Diff touches 3 production files (IoUtil.java, AgentServlet.java, JolokiaHttpHandler.java) plus 2 test files (AgentServletTest.java, IoUtilTest.java). The core change is a new `IoUtil.checkCallbackSafe(String)` static method using regex `^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*(\.[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*|\[[0-9]+\])*$` which accepts plain identifiers, dotted paths, and numeric array-index access — a reasonable superset of real-world JSONP callback names (jQuery, AngularJS style) while rejecting payloads with parens, semicolons, whitespace, angle brackets, newlines. It's called: (1) inside IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose before writing the callback — this is the shared sink for both agent flavors' streaming paths; (2) in AgentServlet.sendAllJSON before concatenating callback+json; (3) in JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON before the same concatenation. This covers all sink sites identified in the alert/exploiter evidence, including the ParsedUri-decoded callback values (since JolokiaHttpHandler reads via ParsedUri.getParameter() regardless of which parseQuery branch populated it, and validation occurs at the point of use). The added tests exercise both accept and reject cases directly on checkCallbackSafe and end-to-end through the real doGet()/streamResponseAndClose entry points, mirroring existing test patterns. No unrelated behavior changes; no broad refactors; no weakening/removal of functionality. The exception propagates uncaught through doGet/doHandle (documented as a known risk — legitimate JSONP clients unaffected since their callback names satisfy the pattern), which is an acceptable trade-off for a security fix and doesn't leave meaningful residual risk.
output_json.pov_result: Before patch: POV exits 0, response body begins with unescaped `alert(String.fromCharCode(88,83,83))//(` confirming JSONP callback XSS. After patch (independently reproduced): POV exits 1 with `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Invalid callback name given...` thrown from IoUtil.checkCallbackSafe via streamResponseAndClose → AgentServlet.sendStreamingResponse → sendResponse → handle → doGet, i.e. the vulnerability no longer reproduces and no malicious content is written before rejection.
output_json.regression_result: Independently reran `mvn -B -pl agent/core -am test -Dtest=IoUtilTest,AgentServletTest`: Tests run: 30, Failures: 0, Errors: 0. Orchestrator logs additionally show a full `mvn -B -pl agent/core -am test` run (486 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors) and a full reactor `mvn install -DskipTests` across agent/core + agent/jvm succeeding (confirms JolokiaHttpHandler.java compiles cleanly). The agent/jvm module's own JolokiaHttpHandlerTest failures are documented as pre-existing/unrelated (reproduced identically on unpatched baseline via git stash, caused by a JDK-specific NPE in com.sun.net.httpserver.Headers.put unrelated to this change), so they don't affect this verdict.
output_json.summary: The patch adds a shared JSONP callback validator (IoUtil.checkCallbackSafe) enforcing a safe JS-reference-expression regex, and calls it at all three sink sites named in the alert: the shared streaming sink IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose (covers both AgentServlet's and JolokiaHttpHandler's streaming paths, including both ParsedUri decoding branches since validation happens at the sink, not the source), AgentServlet.sendAllJSON (non-streaming servlet path), and JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON (non-streaming JVM-agent path). Invalid callback values throw IllegalArgumentException before any response bytes are written, preventing partial/malicious content leakage. I independently reran the POV against the patched worktree via the docker wrapper and confirmed it no longer reproduces (exits 1 with the expected IllegalArgumentException), and independently reran the targeted regression suite (IoUtilTest, AgentServletTest: 30/30 passing). The orchestrator's broader regression run (486 tests, full agent/core suite, plus reactor install across agent/core+agent/jvm) also passed. The diff is minimal and scoped to the vulnerability; the POV file itself was only added, not modified, by the patch.
